response.sql: WITH group_avgs AS (SELECT rfistat, AVG(modindex) AS avg_modindex FROM signals GROUP BY rfistat), valid AS (SELECT rfistat, avg_modindex FROM group_avgs WHERE avg_modindex IS NOT NULL), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_modindex) AS base FROM valid), kept AS (SELECT v.rfistat, v.avg_modindex, v.avg_modindex - b.base AS above_baseline FROM valid v CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE v.avg_modindex > b.base), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_modindex) AS km FROM kept) SELECT k.rfistat, k.avg_modindex, k.above_baseline, ABS(k.avg_modindex - m.km) AS diff_from_kept_mean FROM kept k CROSS JOIN kept_mean m;

assumptions.assumption: Signals with a NULL rfistat form their own group, and AVG(modindex) skips NULL modindex values within each group.
Only NULL counts as 'no status'. Empty-string rfistat values would form a separate group, not be merged with the NULL group.
A group whose modindex values are all NULL has no average. It is excluded from the baseline and from the kept statuses.
'How far it differs from the mean of the kept averages' is the absolute difference, ABS(avg - mean of kept averages).
The baseline is the unweighted mean of the per-status averages, and a status is kept only if its average is strictly greater than the baseline.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat the no-status group as not a status at all: exclude signals with NULL rfistat from the grouping, so it is not included in the baseline or the kept results.

alternatives.interpretation: 'How far it differs' is a signed difference: avg minus the mean of the kept averages, so values below that mean come out negative.
